content:
Maria: quick follow-up to the authn/authz RFC — thinking about the sentinel proxy + delegation shape. can we sync on remaining open questions?
Jordan: skimmed the RFC. two things stood out: token lifetime semantics, and how we surface audit/span for proxied requests.
Ben: my practical bias: short-lived delegation tokens (5m-ish) bound to both proxy and actor. avoid issuing long-lived cross-project keys.
Rahul: question: how does the API express the acting identity? header (X-Acting-Actor) vs ephemeral JWT claim?
Eva: jwt claim + signature gives better audit and tamper-resistance. but we need a revocation story. otherwise revoked service still works until expiry.
Maria: revocation sets per-project are heavy. alternative: very short TTL + refresh via mTLS from the proxy, avoid DB check on every request.
SRE-Bot: incident note: proxy-minted token expired unexpectedly in prod-1 at 2025-11-02T04:12Z, caused a 30s window of 502s.
Jordan: we need a retry/refresh behaviour: proxy should attempt refresh on 401 for idempotent calls. but that doesn't cover streams.
Ben: streaming is the tricky bit — retries aren't possible. options: (a) keep streaming requests on long-lived project-scoped tokens, (b) server-side hold of client identity (two-phase: accept, then stream). both have tradeoffs.
Maria: two-phase increases tail latency and implementation complexity. prefer (a) for streaming-critical flows: mint a constrained streaming token derived from long-term credential with explicit KMS wrapping, and strict audit.
Rahul: proto token claim example (WIP):
```json
{
  "iss": "redwood-proxy",
  "sub": "svc:billing",
  "actor": "user:alice",
  "scope": "project:acme:invoke",
  "stream": true,
  "exp": 1740000000
}
```
Jordan: looks ok. we should standardize claim names (iss/sub/actor/scope/exp/stream) and include a minting_id so revocations/forensics can link back to the proxy event.
Eva: RBAC mapping note: prefer role->capability instead of sprawling resource-permission matrix. map roles to capabilities (invoke-model, manage-keys, read-audit) and then project-scoped tokens grant specific capability set. simpler for product teams.
Maria: migration proposal (two-phase): phase 1: proxy-only delegation for new service onboarding (no long-lived keys). phase 2 (after 3 months observation): allow explicit project-scoped streaming keys for whitelisted services with extra auditing.
Jordan: console + flag needed: `allow_long_stream_keys` per-project + audit event on mint. KMS wrapping required (HSM/KMS envelope).
Ben: action items: 1) update RFC with token schema + TTL defaults 2) prototype refresh flow in proxy 3) add minting audit event + minting_id 4) console flag + docs for platform teams
Maria: I will update the RFC draft tonight. who volunteers for prototype + CLI bits? @Ben @Rahul?
Ben: +1 i'll own the prototype. will sketch akka/netty flow and refresh path.
Rahul: i'll take the CLI and token format tests. ETA end of week.
Eva: :thumbsup:
Maria: thanks — i'll incorporate the decisions and we can lock RFC v2 once Ben sends a short POC.
Jordan: one more open question: impersonation surface. do we allow full actor impersonation or only act-as with audit link? i prefer act-as + immutable audit event.
Ben: agreed, no silent impersonation. every delegated token must carry `minting_id` and `proxy_mtls_cert` references for traceability.
Maria: cool. that's enough for now, i'll add a checklist to RFC.
